title: Understatement and Milestones: Llegar a + Infinitive

sections.content:
You know *llegar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 25 for a result reached after effort, an extreme, or a *si* clause (*si llega a llover*). In testimony and chronicles, *llegar a* is especially useful in three nuanced forms.

1. **Negated understatement (*no llegar a* + infinitive):** softens a claim to 'never quite' or 'did not go so far as to': *Nunca llegó a sentirse forastero* ('He never quite came to feel like an outsider'); *El recelo inicial no llegó a romper la convivencia* ('The initial wariness never went so far as to break coexistence').
2. **Recurring extremes (*llegaba a* + infinitive):** in the imperfect, *llegar a* describes repeated highs or lows during a past period: *En invierno llegaba a trabajar doce horas seguidas*.
3. **Prior milestone (*había llegado a* + infinitive):** in the pluperfect, it marks a stage of belonging or mastery already reached before a later turning point: *Para entonces ya había llegado a echar raíces en el puerto*.

sections.title: Nuances of llegar a + infinitive in testimony
rows: No llegaron a perder su lengua materna.
Negated preterite: 'never went so far as to lose'.
Nunca llegó a sentirse un forastero en el barrio.
En aquellos años llegaba a reunir a veinte vecinos en su mesa.
Antes de jubilarse ya había llegado a echar raíces allí.

items.spanish: Gracias a la hospitalidad del barrio, los recién llegados no llegaron a sentirse forasteros.
items.english: Thanks to the hospitality of the neighbourhood, the newcomers never came to feel like outsiders.

items.spanish: Aunque habló otro idioma en la escuela, nunca llegó a olvidar su lengua materna.
items.english: Although she spoke another language at school, she never came to forget her mother tongue.

items.spanish: En los primeros inviernos, el recelo de algunos comerciantes llegaba a dificultar el alquiler.
items.english: In the first winters, the wariness of some shopkeepers even went so far as to make renting difficult.

items.spanish: Cuando le ofrecieron trasladarse a otra ciudad, ya había llegado a sentir un profundo apego por el puerto.
items.english: When they offered him a move to another city, he had already come to feel a deep attachment to the port.

sections.content: Do not drop the preposition *a* between *llegar* and the infinitive: write *no llegó a entender* and *había llegado a echar raíces*, never *no llegó entender*. Also keep *no llegar a* + infinitive distinct from *no poder* + infinitive: *no llegó a perderla* states that things never went that far, not that the person lacked the ability.
